title: With gradio==4.18.0, only get loading screen for server for remote connections going through nginx
body: With gradio==4.18.0, remote connections through nginx only show a loading screen. The same app works locally and through the raw IP and port. The exact same code works through nginx with gradio==4.17.0, so switching between 4.17.0 and 4.18.0 consistently changes the result. This is blocking my usage.

symptoms_visible: With Gradio 4.18.0, the app only shows a loading screen when I open it remotely through nginx.
The same app loads through its raw IP and port, and switching back to Gradio 4.17.0 makes the nginx URL work again.
N0.label: N0 nginx-only loading failure reported

symptoms_visible: At the HTTPS nginx URL, my browser blocks requests to http://xxxx.ai/info and http://xxxx.ai/theme.css as mixed content and reports that the API details could not be fetched.
A small Blocks chatbot app also has the proxy-page errors, while direct port access loads normally and has no console errors.
N1.label: N1 mixed-content errors reproduced

symptoms_visible: The raw HTTP IP-and-port URL displays the app, but the HTTPS DNS URL through nginx does not.
The nginx configuration already forwards Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP.
N2.label: N2 nginx reproduction supplied

symptoms_visible: After installing the supplied candidate Gradio build, the trivial app and the full h2oGPT app both load through my nginx DNS URL.
I tried several things in the full app and did not notice the previous proxy-page problem.
N3.label: N3 candidate build verified on reporter nginx

symptoms_visible: On a Gradio build containing the correction, both the simple app and h2oGPT load normally through my HTTPS nginx URL instead of remaining on the loading screen.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter nginx path resolved

question_patterns: Could you open the browser developer console on the failing page and paste any errors?
What network or console errors appear while the loading screen is shown?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the bad 4.18.0 case, the page is loaded from https://xxxx.ai/, but the console says requests to http://xxxx.ai/info and http://xxxx.ai/theme.css are blocked as mixed content. It also says 'Could not get api details: Failed to fetch' and 'Unable to preload CSS'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There are no mixed-content or failed-request errors; all resources return successfully and the page remains on the loading screen after rendering.
The same blocked /info and theme.css requests appear, but the browser formats the console messages differently.

question_patterns: Can you share the Gradio app code or reduce it to a small example?
Does a minimal Blocks app show the same behavior through the proxy?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My full app is h2oGPT. I also launched a small Blocks app with a Chatbot, Textbox and submit callback on 0.0.0.0. It behaves somewhat differently but still badly through nginx and produces the same blocked http://xxxx.ai/info and http://xxxx.ai/theme.css errors. Direct port access to that app is good and produces no console errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A minimal Gradio app works normally through the same nginx URL; only h2oGPT shows the problem.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c2-c7: pseudotensor supplied browser-console output and a minimal Blocks app after requests from pngwn and abidlabs. The answer preserves the reporter's raw errors and observations; identifying the proxy-origin regression remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Could you share a reproducible nginx configuration and the results from its raw and proxied URLs?
What headers does your nginx location forward, and how do the direct and proxy URLs behave?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I set up an nginx case. Its location proxies to the raw server and sets Host $host, X-Forwarded-Scheme $scheme, X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme, X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr, X-Real-IP $remote_addr, Upgrade, Connection and HTTP/1.1. The raw URL http://52.0.25.199:14051/ displays the app, while the proxy DNS URL https://<redacted-host>/ shows the broken loading page and console errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The nginx configuration does not send Host or X-Forwarded-Proto, and adding those headers makes the HTTPS proxy URL work without changing Gradio.
The same header configuration and raw-good/proxy-bad behavior reproduce on different hostnames and ports.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c3 and c11: pseudotensor created the requested nginx reproduction and supplied its configuration plus raw-versus-proxy observations. The later Runpod deployment belongs to participant3 and is deliberately not merged into this reporter's causal chain.

question_patterns: Could you install this candidate Gradio build and report what happens through the same nginx URL?
Please test the supplied wheel with both the small reproduction and your full application.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yup, that works. The simple app loads through the proxy. I also tried the full h2oGPT app with the shared 4.18.0 build and it seems all good now. I played around with a few things and don't notice any issues, so it looks back to the 4.17.0 behavior.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The supplied build still requests /info and theme.css over http and remains on the loading screen through my nginx URL.
The supplied build works through nginx for both apps, but the first page load is slightly slower than with 4.17.0.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c18-c22: this is pre-landing candidate-build verification. Pseudotensor installed the supplied wheel, first tested the small app and then h2oGPT, and confirmed the original nginx loading failure was gone. participant3's later failure on Runpod is a different proxy deployment and is not substituted for this result.

solution.intent: Use and ship a Gradio build that corrects the 4.18 reverse-proxy URL regression so an application reached through an HTTPS nginx origin requests its API details and theme assets through the public HTTPS origin rather than insecure HTTP URLs.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the reporter's working nginx forwarding setup and update to a Gradio build containing the candidate correction. Verify that the nginx HTTPS URL loads /info and theme.css without blocked HTTP requests and that both the minimal app and h2oGPT render normally.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the version comparison, nginx headers, blocked HTTP resource URLs and candidate-build result. Concluding that Gradio 4.18's public-origin handling behind the TLS-terminating proxy generated the insecure resource URLs is engineer inference. The separate Runpod discussion eventually identified an incorrectly preserved Host header on that provider, but that is not the accepted diagnosis for pseudotensor's nginx setup, whose unchanged configuration worked with the candidate Gradio build.

edges.comment: Reporter resolution, c18-c23: abidlabs supplied a candidate wheel and pseudotensor confirmed both the minimal app and h2oGPT behaved like 4.17.0 through nginx. The audio issue raised later in c34 was moved to a separate issue and is an independent problem, so it is not chained onto this resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the resolved problem as a Gradio 4.18 reverse-proxy URL regression that caused an HTTPS nginx page to request /info and theme.css through insecure HTTP URLs, which browsers blocked as mixed content.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the 4.17-versus-4.18 comparison, raw-port-versus-nginx comparison, browser-console output, supplied nginx reproduction and successful candidate-build test.

The final recommendation must use a Gradio build containing the reverse-proxy correction; direct raw-port access or downgrading may be acknowledged as temporary workarounds but not presented as the fix.
Must not substitute the later Runpod Host-header diagnosis for the reporter's nginx root cause; that evidence came from a different operator and deployment.
Must have the reporter verify the correction through the same HTTPS nginx path on the candidate or another build containing the fix before declaring the original loading-screen issue resolved.
Must not fold the later gr.Audio playback problem into this diagnostic chain because the thread moved it to a separate issue.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical application developer who manages Python environments, remote servers and a large Gradio application; can reduce the problem to a small script and arrange an nginx reproduction, but does not claim nginx expertise.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, evidence-driven and cooperative; provides exact versions, code, console logs, server URLs and configuration when requested, then tests candidate builds promptly and reports practical results.
